Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. China led with 132 golds, followed by japan with 41, south korea with 21 and uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’ special judge dig vinay singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on october 9. The appeal challenges the august 3 order of the rouse avenue court, brij bhushan and vinod tomar in the case.

Article Title: 'No time to experiment': Captain Shubman Gill wants all resources available for India's ODI World Cup prep
Article Text:
India's Rohit Sharma and skipper Shubman Gill (ANI Photo)

Kamboj, Nabi on trial for No. 8 spot

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fielding woes

New Chandigarh: If one takes a quick scan of India’s ODI resources for next year’s World Cup in South Africa, the pace cupboard wears a bare and fragile look. There’s only Jasprit Bumrah who truly commands a place in the XI. The rest are either on trial or nursing injuries. Mohammed Siraj has gone off the boil dramatically, losing the confidence of the team management. The other ‘experienced’ pacer in the ranks, Prasidh Krishna, was still in the process of establishing his credentials before breaking down in the second ODI. TOI understands that the team management has identified Gurnoor Brar as a strong prospect in South African conditions.It’s been a rough initiation into ODI captaincy for Shubman Gill . It’s been a year since he assumed the role, but he is yet to get all of his first-choice resources at his disposal. “It’s been unfortunate with the injuries and with the scheduling. We have not been able to play the bowling line-up that we would like to. It’s a great chance for them to showcase their skills,” Gill said after the series win over West Indies here on Saturday.The anxiety was apparent, though. He declared the need for urgency in sorting out the ODI core. With Bumrah away playing in the Asian Games, this series was meant to check the second line of pacers.But Gill doesn’t seem to be in any mood to be in the experimental phase. “I honestly think there is not that much time to experiment. The combination that we want to play, hopefully we get all the players that are available from the next series. The combination that we would like to play in the World Cup, we want to start playing with that combination,” he stated.Here’s the catch. The next series is a five-ODI affair in New Zealand, which will be followed by a two-Test series. Precariously placed in the World Test Championship table, the team management intends to pull out the Test regulars after the third ODI. That would mean Bumrah, Krishna and Siraj will not be available for the entire series. There’s a strong chance Brar, too, could be pulled out.Pace bowling was India’s biggest asset in the last two World Cups. Bumrah, Mohammed Shami, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Siraj were incisive with the new ball and potent in the death overs. Gill clearly sees the gap in his bowling attack.“Bowling in the power play and in the death have hurt us. If you don’t get off to a good start in the power play, it’s not easy to take wickets in the middle overs. It’s not easy to create chances with only four fielders outside the ring. The intensity of the game is completely different if you don’t keep taking wickets either in the power play or in the middle overs. That’s why this series has been so high scoring. Even today we lost two wickets in the power play but we still managed to get 350 on the board,” Gill spelt out his concerns.It’s not just about the new-ball bowlers. Gill also revealed that the team management is looking for a pacer who can be a capable batter at No. 8. Recurring injuries to Harshit Rana have compounded Gill’s problems. Which is why Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj were handed debuts in this series.“Anshul and Auqib are going to be in the mix a lot. Anshul is someone who can also bat at No. 8. And that number is very crucial for us. We don’t know who will be fit at the World Cup. And if we want someone who can bowl and can bat a bit at No. 8, Anshul can do the job. And even Aqib can bat a bit and do the job. So, we want to see which players can deliver under pressure,” Gill said.Both Kamboj and Nabi endured rough debuts, conceding runs at over nine runs per over. However, this is the only spot where Gill may be willing to bide his time.“They would have liked to have done a much better job. But you know, a little bit harsh on them. It’s not easy to come and to be able to deliver straight away. I hope that they learn from their mistakes and the opportunities that they get,” Gill said.Gill also made his displeasure about the fielding standards of the team clear. The Indian team’s fielding has worsened over the last eight months.“We dropped around three or four catches today. I don’t think Shai was dropped but still dropping three or four catches breaks the momentum of the team. Our fielding in the series, I would say, has not been up to the mark. I think in the whole series we dropped around seven catches, if I am not wrong. And even in the field today we gave away, many times in the field we were quite sloppy,” he said.“I think leading up to the World Cup, these are the areas where we definitely need to get better at. We need to be at the peak of our powers, especially when we are in the field. It’s not easy for the bowlers, so the fielders can help a lot. And if the wicket is not helping much for the bowlers and the fielding being substandard, it’s a difficult job for the bowlers,” he added.
Article Summary: Jasprit bumrah, mohammed shami, bhuvneshwar kumar and mohammed siraj were incisive with the new ball and potent in the death overs. Gill also revealed that the team management is looking for a pacer who can be a capable batter at no. 8. The next series is a five-odi affair in new zealand, followed by a two-test series.

Article Title: EXCLUSIVE | Asian Games gold done, Neeru Dhanda eyes Olympic shotgun medal to end wait since Rajyavardhan Rathore’s 2004 silver

From illness to three medals

Nagoya: From left, India's Manisha Keer, Ashima Ahlawat and Neeru Dhanda pose with the national flag after winning the silver medal. (PTI Photo)

Mission Olympics begins

‘Golden girl’? Neeru loves it

NEW DELHI: Days before leaving for the Asian Games 2026, Neeru Dhanda was hospitalised with viral fever. She had barely any time to recover before boarding the flight to Japan. There was no proper recovery period. Just medicines, ORS, and a dream of winning a medal at the Asian Games.When she reached Aichi-Nagoya and entered her hotel room, Neeru picked up her gun and told herself three words: "Nerru, tu training pe hai (Neeru, you are in training."It was a message she wanted to give her own mind - a way of staying focused and refusing to think about the illness.With water bottles, ORS and medicines by her side, Neeru kept her dream alive. The trap shooter, who had won gold at the ISSF World Cup in Lonato earlier this year, eventually stepped onto the range, loaded her ammunition and shot her way to glory.She finished the Asian Games with three medals - two golds and a silver - emerging as one of India's standout performers.Neeru first won gold in the women's individual trap event. She then teamed up with Manisha Keer and Aashima Ahlawat to win silver in the women's trap team event.On the penultimate day of the shooting competition, she partnered Kynan Chenai to win gold in the trap mixed team event.But behind the three medals was a battle that began even before she reached the shooting range.“I didn't let my mind receive the message that I was sick or unwell. I didn't want to let myself think that I was sick. Whenever I felt down or weak, I used to tell myself loudly, ‘Neeru, tu training pe hai abhi.’ This is what kept me motivated throughout the Asian Games,” Neeru told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.“Honestly, I felt very weak because there was no recovery period after the hospitalisation. I thought about skipping the Games, but no, I am very stubborn. I wanted to do something different. Very few people get this opportunity. I was lucky that I got it, and I am happy that I delivered,” she said.Neeru dedicated her three-medal haul to late Raja Randhir Singh, India's first Asian Games shooting gold medallist, who passed away aged 79 in May. Randhir, a five-time Olympian, had won India's first Asian Games shooting gold in 1978.Neeru had met him a few times and remembered the encouragement he gave her.“I dedicate these medals to late Raja Randhir Singh. He was a lovely soul. I got to meet him a couple of times. Whenever he met me, he blessed me. He always said, ‘Beta, be brave. You are a shooter, you need to be brave. Shoot with bravery, you will get the result.’ Those words helped me a lot in Aichi-Nagoya,” Neeru said."I also want to dedicate to my federation, SAI, SAI Bhopal, Bhopa Shooting Academy where I train, my coaches, and everyone who has been with me throughout this journey," she said.The World Cup is done. The Asian Games are done. Now, Neeru has set her sights on the Los Angeles Olympics. Her immediate target is the World Championship in Doha, which will offer a quota opportunity for the 2028 Olympics.“The moment I leave Japan, my target will shift towards the World Championship in Doha. That is a quota competition for the Los Angeles Olympics, so I will focus on that. That is my ultimate goal. Olympics mein medal jeetna hai,” she said.India have won several Olympic medals in shooting, but the shotgun disciplines have produced only one Olympic medal for the country - Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore's silver in men's double trap at the 2004 Athens Olympics.After her performances in Aichi-Nagoya, Neeru will be one of the Indian shooters attracting attention ahead of the Los Angeles Games.Neeru has also earned the nickname ‘golden girl’ after her recent run of success. Asked about the title, she laughed.“Golden girl title... I just love it. I love this title. I hope it continues to be like this always. It was possible because of the hard work I have put in day and night,” she said.For Neeru, the key has been constantly looking back at her own performances and learning from her mistakes.“Introspection has always helped me. Whenever I do something wrong or make mistakes, I ask myself, ‘Where did I go wrong?’ I get that answer. That helps me a lot,” she said.After returning home with three medals, Neeru was eager to meet her parents and family and celebrate her success with them.But she had only a few hours. Neeru was at her home in Sangatpura village in Jind, speaking to her mother, when she received a call that gave her another reason to return to Japan.Former India shooter and deputy chef de mission Anjali Bhagwat told her that she had been selected as India's women's flag bearer for the closing ceremony of the Asian Games 2026. Within hours, Neeru packed her bags and headed back to the airport.“I got a call from Anjali Bhagwat ma'am. She asked me to be the flag bearer at the closing ceremony. It's a big honour for me. I didn't want to let it go,” Neeru told TimesofIndia.com.Her parents were delighted by the news. “My parents are so happy. When I gave them the news about the closing ceremony, my mother said, ‘Ja beta, mauka nahi milta ye kisi ko. Aaja, phir se khushi manayenge,’” Neeru said.
Article Summary: Neeru dhanda won three medals at the asian games in aichi-nagoya. She dedicated her haul to late raja randhir singh, india's first asian games shooting gold medallist, who passed away aged 79 in may. Neeru has set her sights on the los angeles olympics. Neeru has earned the nickname ‘golden girl’ after her recent run of success.

India fall short of Hangzhou record but finish strongly

India signed off from the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya with a strong fourth-place finish, winning 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.While India fell short of its record-breaking 106-medal haul at the Hangzhou Asian Games, the Aichi-Nagoya campaign was marked by a late surge, several historic firsts and dominant performances in sports such as athletics, shooting, archery, boxing and team events.Around 500 Indian athletes competed at the continental multi-sport event, with the country eventually finishing among the top five in the medal standings.Here is the complete sport-wise medal tally for India at the Asian Games 2026:Archery led the gold-medal standings with five golds. Shooting and boxing followed with three gold medals each, while wrestling contributed two.India also won two gold medals apiece in cricket, hockey and kabaddi, with both men's and women's teams contributing to the country's strong finish.India's medals came across 21 sports, demonstrating the breadth of its performance at the continental event.Alongside the major medal-winning disciplines, India also secured podium finishes in weightlifting, wushu, badminton, kurash, mixed martial arts, rowing, sepaktakraw, soft tennis and table tennis.The 85-medal haul was India's second-highest ever at the Asian Games, behind the record 106 medals won at Hangzhou 2023.India's final tally of 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals secured the country a fourth-place finish in the overall medal standings.Athletics was the backbone of India's medal campaign, producing a wide range of podium finishes across track and field events.India won gold in the women's 4x400m relay, while athletes also collected medals in the 10,000m, 1500m, marathon, shot put, long jump, high jump, javelin throw, pole vault, 400m hurdles, 5000m, 3000m steeplechase, 200m, decathlon and relay events.Gulveer Singh was among India's standout performers, winning silver in the men's 10,000m and 1500m events and bronze in the 5000m.Sawan Berwal won silver in the men's marathon, becoming India's first marathon medallist at the Asian Games since 1982 while also setting a national record.Sarvesh Kushare ended India's 56-year wait for a men's high jump medal, while Baranica Elangovan created history by becoming the first Indian pole vaulter to win an Asian Games medal.Vithya Ramraj added another landmark performance by winning bronze in the women's 400m hurdles and breaking a national record that had stood for 42 years.Shooting once again played a major role in India's Asian Games campaign, contributing 15 medals, including three golds.Neeru Dhanda won India's first individual gold medal of the Games in the women's trap competition. She later combined with Kynan Chenai to win gold in the mixed trap event.Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh also won gold in the mixed team 10m air pistol event, matching the Asian record.India's shooters also collected medals in the 10m air rifle, 50m rifle 3P, 25m pistol, trap and skeet events.Archery was India's most successful sport in terms of gold medals, with five titles.Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Prithika Pradeep and Chikitha Taniparthi won gold in the women's compound team event, while Chikitha Taniparthi and Sahil Jadhav claimed the mixed compound team title.Sahil Jadhav, Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru and Kushal Dalal won the men's compound team gold.The women's recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kumkum Mohod and Kirti Sharma also finished on top.Kumkum then produced one of the defining moments of the Games by winning India's first-ever women's individual recurve gold medal at the Asian Games.India enjoyed a strong showing in boxing, winning three gold medals.Lovlina Borgohain became only the second Indian woman to win an Asian Games boxing gold, following Mary Kom's historic achievement at the 2014 Incheon Games.Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal also won gold medals in their respective categories.India added bronze medals through Narender Berwal, Priya Ghanghas and Kapil Pokhariya.India's wrestlers also made their mark in Aichi-Nagoya.Aman Sehrawat won gold in the men's 57kg category, while Sujeet Kalkal became champion in the men's 65kg event.Nitesh Kumar and Antim Panghal won silver medals, while Sunil Kumar and Deepak Punia added bronze medals.India's team sports produced a spectacular late surge.The men's and women's cricket teams successfully defended their Asian Games titles. The men's team defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the final, while the women's team beat Sri Lanka to retain the gold medal.Hockey also delivered two gold medals.The Indian women's hockey team ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games title, while the men's team, led by Harmanpreet Singh, completed its campaign with a commanding 5-1 victory over Malaysia in the final.The men's hockey gold was India's 21st gold medal of the Games and sealed the country's fourth-place finish.Golf produced another landmark moment for India.Pranavi Urs won the women's individual gold medal, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games gold in golf.India also won silver in the women's team event through Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.Olympic medallist Mirabai Chanu claimed silver in the women's 49kg weightlifting event.It was her first Asian Games medal and ended India's wait for a medal in the sport since the 1998 Bangkok Games.Wushu athlete Roshibina Devi also continued her impressive continental run by winning her third consecutive Asian Games medal, taking silver in the women's 60kg sanda event.India's squash contingent also delivered multiple podium finishes.Abhay Singh and Anahat Singh won silver in the men's and women's singles events respectively.Anahat's silver made her the first Indian woman to win a singles silver medal in squash at the Asian Games.India also won bronze medals in mixed doubles and the men's and women's team events.The Aichi-Nagoya campaign was notable not just for the medal count but also for the number of historic achievements.Kumkum Mohod became the first Indian woman to win individual recurve gold at the Asian Games. Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games golf gold.Suchika Tariyal secured India's first Asian Games medal in mixed martial arts, while Jay Meena became the country's first Asian Games medallist in soft tennis after reaching the men's singles semifinals.India also ended long medal droughts in several athletics disciplines.India's success in Aichi-Nagoya also carried significance for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.India secured Olympic quotas through its performances in archery and hockey. The Asian Games offered Olympic qualification opportunities in seven sports — archery, hockey, sailing, squash, surfing, tennis and triathlon.India secured places in both men's and women's hockey as well as in archery's compound mixed team and women's individual recurve events.India's 85-medal haul was 21 medals fewer than its record 106 at Hangzhou, while the gold-medal count dropped from 28 to 21.However, the final standings did not tell the entire story of India's campaign.As recently as Thursday, India had only 10 gold medals and was outside the top 10 of the medal table. A remarkable late surge changed the complexion of the campaign.India won 12 medals on Friday, including six golds, before adding nine medals on the penultimate day. Gold medals in cricket and hockey, along with individual triumphs in wrestling, archery and golf, propelled India into the top five.The final tally of 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals ensured another top-five Asian Games finish and capped a campaign defined by historic firsts, successful title defences and a powerful finish.India may have fallen short of the Hangzhou record, but Aichi-Nagoya 2026 will be remembered as another landmark Asian Games campaign for Indian sport.

Article Title: Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock China Open exit, falls to Nikola Bartunkova in straight sets

World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shock third-round exit at the China Open on Sunday, losing 6-4, 6-3 to Czech Republic’s Nikola Bartunkova. The 34th-ranked Bartunkova produced one of the biggest upsets of the tournament, defeating the four-time Grand Slam champion in one hour and 34 minutes. The Czech hit four aces and capitalised on Sabalenka’s struggles to close out a straight-sets victory.Sabalenka had five break-point opportunities in the opening set but was unable to convert any of them. Bartunkova, meanwhile, stayed composed on the big points and secured the only break she needed to take the first set 6-4.The Czech continued to dictate the contest in the second set, breaking Sabalenka and maintaining her advantage to close out the match 6-3. The defeat continues Sabalenka’s difficult record at the Beijing tournament. The Belarusian has never progressed beyond the quarterfinals at the China Open.Sabalenka arrived in Beijing looking to bounce back from her US Open disappointment, where she was denied a third consecutive title by Elena Rybakina. However, Rybakina herself suffered a surprise defeat earlier in Beijing, losing to unseeded Alina Charaeva in the second round.The early exits of the top two seeds mean neither Rybakina nor Sabalenka will feature in the latter stages of the WTA 1000 tournament. The China Open is being played on hard courts in Beijing from September 30 to October 11. Bartunkova will next face Austria’s Sinja Kraus, who defeated Ukraine’s Dayana Yastremska 6-1, 6-4.The Czech will now have an opportunity to extend her breakthrough run in Beijing after taking down one of the tournament’s biggest names.In the men’s draw, top seed Alexander Zverev is scheduled to face Novak Djokovic in the quarterfinals. Djokovic reached the last eight after maintaining his perfect record at the China Open, while Zverev entered the clash after progressing through his section of the draw.

The Lakers overhauled their roster this summer, and one starting spot still looks unfinished. Walker Kessler and Quentin Grimes arrived, while LeBron James, Marcus Smart and Deandre Ayton left. Lakers need perimeter defense, secondary rim protection and enough offense to hold up. No one on the roster fits it as a proven power forward, and that probably doesn't change before opening night.Derrick Jones Jr. keeps coming up as the fix. The 6-foot-6 Clippers forward, 29, played one season beside Luka Doncic in Dallas, and a Clippers roster stripped of five first-round picks might listen. Reports published October 3 put him forward as an option. Nothing is agreed, and every idea here is speculation, not word from either front office.Los Angeles has two in-house candidates in newcomers Ziaire Williams and Sandro Mamukelashvili, and either could claim the starting power forward job. Right now, it is fair to say that the newcomer duo is a backup option or a trade asset. Jones would upgrade any in-house option as a proven, veteran two-way contributor. His strength, agility and verticality suit a defender beside Doncic, who can feed him enough quality shots to stay viable on offense.As the summer roster changes happened, it looks like the Lakers are reaching the end of perfecting their team. Still, there are some gaps. "The Lakers need a forward and the Los Angeles Clippers need some draft capital, which makes these two teams the perfect trading partners," Fansided’s Mat Issa wrote. "This one would be another reunion for Dončić from his Finals run with the Dallas Mavericks. Here, the Lakers would trade LaRavia, Dalton Knecht and three second-round picks to get Derrick Jones Jr. "Jones is in the final year of his contract and is not expected to get an extension. The league docked the Clippers five first-round picks, and the forward is believed to be among the veterans on their trade block. Moving him before the deadline would return something, while waiting risks losing him for nothing. Los Angeles could also hang back and wait for Jones to test free agency next summer. The Clippers' asking price is unclear.P.J. Washington in Dallas and Herbert Jones in New Orleans are other names on the radar, and Washington looks like the surer option.Doncic, Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and Quentin Grimes already project as four starters, with one spot open. The clock runs in two directions. Los Angeles will judge Williams and Mamukelashvili over roughly two months, and the Clippers face the trade deadline with an expiring contract. If neither Laker claims the spot, the calls start. If the Clippers sit still, Jones may walk next summer with no return. For now, the Lakers have a name, a paper package and no deal.

The gold rush was not simply a repeat

NEW DELHI: India won 28 gold medals at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. Four years later, the question in Aichi-Nagoya was how many of those titles it could retain. The answer? - Eight, out of the 28 Hangzhou golds. That’s 28.6 per cent of the total. Twenty titles changed hands.The biggest changes came in the sports that had driven India's record campaign in Hangzhou. All seven shooting golds were lost, while all six athletics titles changed hands and, India also failed to retain either of its two individual compound archery golds.But just the gold-medal count does not tell the whole story. India retained the three compound team archery titles, both kabaddi golds, both cricket titles and the men's hockey crown.The other golds came from a different mix of events and athletes. Some had won silver or bronze in Hangzhou and moved up to gold in Japan. Others won titles in events where India had not been on the podium four years earlier.So while 20 of India's 28 Hangzhou champions failed to retain their titles, the gold medals themselves were replaced from a much wider pool. The Aichi-Nagoya campaign, in that sense, was less about defending the Hangzhou haul and more about how India's medal map had changed in four years.While Shooting had produced seven golds and 22 medals for India at Hangzhou, In Aichi-Nagoya, the overall medal tally fell to 15. The gold count dropped from seven to three, while silver moved from nine to eight and bronze from six to four. The biggest change was that none of India's seven Hangzhou golds was defended in the same event.Instead, India found gold elsewhere. Neeru Dhanda won the women's trap individual title and then partnered Kynan Chenai to win mixed trap. Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh added the mixed 10m air pistol gold.The rifle teams that had delivered two of India's Hangzhou golds - men's 10m air rifle and men's 50m rifle 3 Positions - returned with silver in Japan. There was also a new medal in mixed skeet. Anantjeet Singh Naruka and Parinaaz Dhaliwal won bronze, giving India its first Asian Games medal in the event.So while India's shooting haul was smaller in Aichi-Nagoya, the change was not just in the numbers. The seven golds from Hangzhou were gone, and the three titles in Japan came from a different set of events.While India won 29 athletics medals in Hangzhou, Four years later, the tally in Aichi-Nagoya was 24. The bigger change, though, came in the gold count.Six golds in Hangzhou became one in Japan and that lone title came in the women's 4x400m relay, four years after India's men's relay team had won gold in Hangzhou. Silver medals fell from 14 to nine, while bronze medals increased from nine to 14.There was still plenty of continuity among India's medallists. Murali Sreeshankar again won silver in the long jump. Tajinderpal Singh Toor, the Hangzhou gold medallist, finished with silver this time. Tejaswin Shankar moved from silver to bronze in the decathlon, while Ancy Sojan retained her long-jump silver.Vithya Ramraj again won bronze in the 400m hurdles. Gulveer Singh improved on his Hangzhou performance in the 10,000m, moving from bronze to silver. He also added silver in the 1500m and bronze in the 5000m.So the athletics podium did not disappear in Aichi-Nagoya. India still won 23 medals outside gold. The difference was that performances that had produced six titles in Hangzhou produced only one gold four years later.India matched its Hangzhou tally in archery, winning nine medals again - five gold, two silver and two bronze. The medal distribution, however, changed considerably.The three compound team golds were retained and beyond those events, India had a different set of medal-winning performances in Aichi-Nagoya, particularly in the women's recurve events.Kumkum Mohod won individual recurve gold, while the women's recurve team moved from bronze in Hangzhou to gold in Japan. That left the overall numbers unchanged, but the events behind those numbers were different.The individual compound events also saw a change. India had won medals in both the men's and women's individual compound events in Hangzhou. In Aichi-Nagoya, the men's individual compound event was the notable gap.Boxing went in the opposite direction to shooting and athletics. India had returned from Hangzhou with four medals - one silver and three bronze - but no gold, but In Aichi-Nagoya, the haul rose to six, including three gold medals.Lovlina Borgohain upgraded her silver in the women's 75kg category in 2023, to gold four years later, while Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal added two more titles in categories where India had not won gold at Hangzhou. The bronze tally remained unchanged at three.Wrestling also finished with six medals, the same tally as Hangzhou. But the distribution changed completely. India had won one silver and five bronze medals in 2022, without a gold. In Aichi-Nagoya, that became two golds, two silvers and two bronze medals.Aman Sehrawat and Sujeet Kalkal supplied the two freestyle golds, while Nitesh, added a historic silver in Greco-Roman, and Antim Panghal upgraded her bronze from the 2022 Games to silver in 2026.The bronze tally fell from five to two (Sunil Kumar and Deepak Punia), but India added two golds and one silver.Squash finished with five medals in both Hangzhou and Aichi-Nagoya. But the two golds from 2022 were gone.India's tally changed from two gold, one silver and two bronze to two silver and three bronze. Abhay Singh retained the men's singles silver, replacing Saurav Ghosal on the podium. Anahat Singh added a women's singles medal.The men's team and mixed doubles titles from Hangzhou slipped to bronze in Japan. The women's team retained its bronze, while the mixed-team bronze was not repeated. The overall medal count stayed at five. The two golds did not.India had won all four golds available across the two sports in Hangzhou - the men's and women's cricket titles and the men's and women's kabaddi titles and it repeated that sweep in Japan.In the kabaddi double, both Indian teams came through against Iran in the finals, with the women winning 37-34 and the men 40-34. For the women's team, the victory extended an impressive Asian Games record. India has now won the women's kabaddi gold at every edition it has entered except the 2018 Jakarta Games, when Iran took the title and India settled for silver. The 2026 victory was therefore its fourth gold in five appearances.The men's side has an even longer record. India's 40-34 win over Iran was its ninth Asian Games gold in the men's event across 10 editions. The only time it failed to win the title was in 2018, when Iran took gold. India had returned to the top at Hangzhou and retained the crown in Nagoya.Cricket followed with its own repeat. India's women's team opened the 2026 Games by defending the title it had won at Hangzhou, beating Sri Lanka in the final. The men's team then completed the cricket double on October 3, beating Pakistan to retain the men's gold as well.Hockey produced two very different stories in Aichi-Nagoya. The men's gold was defended. The women's bronze became gold.For the men's team, the 2026 title was significant beyond the medal itself. India beat Malaysia 5-1 in the final to retain the Asian Games crown for the first time, becoming only the second country after Pakistan to win consecutive men's hockey golds. The victory also secured direct qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.The women's title was a different story altogether. India had finished with bronze in Hangzhou. In Japan, it beat defending champions China 1-0 to win the Asian Games gold for the first time since 1982. The victory ended a 44-year wait for gold and also secured direct qualification for LA 2028.It also produced a first for Indian hockey at the Asian Games. For the first time, both the men's and women's teams won gold at the same edition.At Hangzhou, Aditi Ashok won silver, giving India its first women's golf medal at the Asian Games. Four years later, Pranavi Urs went one better.She won individual gold, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games golf title. Urs then joined Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar to win India's first women's team medal in the sport. India's overall golf haul doubled from one medal in Hangzhou to two in Aichi-Nagoya.The individual gold also ended a 24-year wait for India. Shiv Kapur had won the men's title in 2002; Pranavi became the first Indian golfer since then to win an individual Asian Games gold.Sailing: Three medals again, but different eventsSailing produced the same number of medals in both editions. India won three medals in Hangzhou and three again in Aichi-Nagoya. But the events behind those medals changed.Two new skiff events produced podium finishes in Japan, replacing the men's windsurfer and men's dinghy medals from Hangzhou. The women's dinghy medal also changed colour, from silver to bronze.Badminton saw one of India's biggest drops between Hangzhou and Aichi-Nagoya. The medal tally fell from three to one. India's 2022 haul included Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty's men's doubles gold, the men's team silver and HS Prannoy's singles bronze.Four years later, the men's team remained India's only podium finisher. But even that medal changed colour, with the silver becoming bronze.Neither of the two individual medals from Hangzhou was defended. There was no individual podium finish in Aichi-Nagoya, leaving India with just one medal from a sport that had produced three in the previous edition.Rowing's fall was even more pronounced. Five medals in Hangzhou became one bronze in Aichi-Nagoya. In 2022, India had taken two silver and three bronze medals across five events. In Japan, only Satnam Singh and Salman Khan's men's double sculls reached the podium.None of the five events that had delivered medals at Hangzhou did so again. And the build-up itself was unsettled, with last-minute changes to crew combinations and event entries. Arvind Singh, a 2022 silver medallist in the lightweight double sculls, was moved into the quadruple sculls, while Balraj Panwar shifted from the quadruple to the single sculls.Tennis went from two medals in Hangzhou to none in Aichi-Nagoya. The bigger change was the end of India's 36-year medal streak at the Asian Games.India had continued to find tennis medals across different generations, from Leander Paes and Mahesh Bhupathi to Sania Mirza, Rohan Bopanna and the current doubles players. That run ended in Japan.India had three quarterfinal opportunities but could not convert any of them into a medal. Sumit Nagal went out in the singles quarterfinals, while India did not have a women's singles entry. The result was India's first medal-less Asian Games tennis campaign since 1986.Equestrian went from two medals in Hangzhou to none in Aichi-Nagoya. India had won one gold and one bronze in 2022. There was no podium finish this time.The campaign was also affected by selection disputes, the absence of an approved show-jumping team and a setback in eventing. The result was a complete reversal from Hangzhou, with a two-medal haul turning into none in Japan.Aichi-Nagoya also added two new sports to India's Asian Games medal list. Suchika Tariyal won bronze in the women's traditional MMA 60kg category, giving India its first Asian Games medal in mixed martial arts.Jay Meena added another first in soft tennis, winning bronze in men's singles. For Meena, the medal came after two previous Asian Games appearances without a podium finish. He had competed at the 2018 and 2022 Games but returned without a medal on both occasions. In Nagoya, he finally reached the podium.Neither medal replaced a gold lost from Hangzhou. They came from sports that had not previously contributed an Asian Games medal to India.Weightlifting produced another long-gap story. Mirabai Chanu's silver in the women's 49kg category was India's first Asian Games weightlifting medal since Karnam Malleswari's silver at Bangkok 1998.There was also a personal milestone. Chanu had Olympic and World Championship medals and Commonwealth Games titles, but an Asian Games medal had remained missing. The silver in Nagoya completed the collection.India had not won a kurash medal at the previous Asian Games. Pincky Balhara put the sport back on India's medal list in Aichi-Nagoya, winning bronze in the women's -78kg category. It was a return to the podium rather than a title defence, adding another sport to India's 2026 medal tally.Wushu, Table Tennis, sepak takraw: Medals from the wider fieldWushu again produced a medal through Roshibina Devi, who won silver in the women's 60kg sanda - her third Asian Games medal.Table tennis added bronze through Diya Chitale and Manush Shah in mixed doubles, while World No.3 men’s pair of Manush Shah and Manav Thakar flattered to deceive.India also retained its bronze in sepak takraw, with the men's quadrant team finishing on the podium again.The other side: Four sports drop out of India's medal listThe Hangzhou-to-Aichi-Nagoya comparison also has a different side. Some sports that had contributed medals in 2022 did not produce one in Japan.Chess, bridge, roller sports and canoeing had together contributed six medals to India's Hangzhou tally - two silver in chess, one silver in bridge, two bronze in roller sports and one bronze in canoeing. None of those four sports were part of the Aichi-Nagoya programme.The changing medal map also showed up in the number of firsts India recorded in Aichi-Nagoya.Thirteen of India's 2026 gold medals came from events in which India had either won silver or bronze at Hangzhou, or had not won a medal at all. That included three shooting golds.The mixed 10m air pistol moved from silver to gold, while Neeru Dhanda won the women's individual trap and mixed trap titles in events where India had not won gold in Hangzhou.Athletics produced another upgrade, with the women's 4x400m relay moving from silver to gold.Archery's women's recurve team went from bronze to gold, while Kumkum Mohod added the individual recurve title.Boxing produced three more. Lovlina Borgohain moved from silver to gold in the women's 75kg category. Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal won titles in categories where India had not taken gold in Hangzhou.Wrestling followed the same pattern. Sujeet Kalkal won the men's 65kg title, while Aman Sehrawat moved from bronze in 2022 to gold in the 57kg category.In golf, Pranavi Urs turned Aditi Ashok's women's individual silver from Hangzhou into gold. Women's hockey completed another major upgrade, moving from bronze in Hangzhou to gold in Aichi-Nagoya.Taken together, these 13 golds explain why the 2026 campaign cannot be judged simply by counting how many Hangzhou champions retained their titles.India did lose 20 of its 28 Hangzhou golds, but several of those losses were replaced by athletes who had finished lower on the podium in 2022, or had not reached it at all.The fact that India defended only eight of its 28 Hangzhou golds does not mean the 2026 campaign simply replaced the previous one with a broader or better model. Hangzhou had a heavy concentration of gold at the top. Shooting won seven. Athletics won six. Archery won five. Together, those three disciplines accounted for 18 of India's 28 gold medals in 2022. That made Hangzhou's medal profile very different from Aichi-Nagoya.And the disciplines that lost the most golds in Japan did not disappear from the podium. Shooting remained one of India's biggest medal contributors with 15 medals. Athletics produced 24, while archery matched its Hangzhou total of nine. So the change was not that India's traditional strengths stopped producing medals. They simply produced fewer golds.
Article Summary: India won 28 gold medals at the 2022 asian games in hangzhou. Four years later, the question in aichi-nagoya was how many titles it could retain. The answer? Eight, out of the 28 of the total of india’s golds. All seven shooting golds were lost, while all six athletics titles changed hands.

Article Title: Asian Games hockey official Gurinder Sangha leaves Japan amid sexual misconduct complaints
Article Text:
India's women's hockey team at Asian Games

Kolkata: Gurinder Singh Sangha, a Jalandhar-based international hockey umpire and technical official who was appointed by the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) as umpire manager for the hockey competition at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, has left Japan before the tournament concluded following multiple complaints of alleged sexual misconduct against him.Sources alleged that Sangha misbehaved with a female hockey official from Malaysia.“A Malaysian official has complained that he tried to hug and kiss her in the name of mentoring, and he has had to leave the Asian Games in Nagoya midway, Hockey India leadership is having conversations about starting an investigation,” said a Hockey India official.The HI official said the latest allegations had once again raised questions about Sangha's conduct and the handling of earlier complaints against him.Meanwhile, Asima Ali, Hockey India vice-president and executive member, welcomed the development.“There can be no tolerance for any form of sexual misconduct in sport. The message has to be clear that complaints will be taken seriously and acted upon promptly. We must be stern in our dealing with such offenders and ensure that the sport remains a safe environment for everyone,” said Ali.Multiple sources also alleged that Sangha, who has previously officiated at major events, including the Asian Games, Olympic qualifiers and the Asia Cup, behaved inappropriately with a member of the hotel staff and showed her obscene videos in his room.The latest complaint is not the first allegation levelled against Sangha. During the Hockey India League in Ranchi in January 2025, a female umpire filed a formal complaint against him while he was serving as Umpires' Manager. Hockey India subsequently confirmed receipt of the complaint and constituted a three-member committee to conduct a preliminary investigation into the matter.According to the complaint, the umpire alleged that Sangha's conduct during an interaction at the team hotel in Ranchi on January 20, 2025, was "unwanted and inappropriate" and left her uncomfortable.In a communication dated Jan 21, 2025, Bhola Nath Singh, secretary general of Hockey India, informed stakeholders that a three-member panel had been constituted in consultation with the federation's Internal Complaint Committee for Prevention of Sexual Harassment to carry out a preliminary investigation and submit its report within two days.The latest episode comes amid increased scrutiny of misconduct complaints within Indian hockey. Earlier this year, Hockey India removed a support staff member from a national camp after harassment allegations surfaced against him, stating that action had been taken immediately after the matter came to its notice.The federation has also grappled with other complaints in recent times, including an April 2026 complaint alleging sexual harassment and abuse of authority by a Hockey India official, and a 2025 case involving misconduct allegations against a junior women's team coach.During the inaugural Women's Hockey India League, a coach was also removed overnight after authorities were informed of harassment complaints involving younger players.
Article Summary: Gurinder singh sangha has left japan before the tournament concluded. Sources alleged that sangha misbehaved with a female hockey official from malaysia. The latest complaint is not the first allegation levelled against sangha. A female umpire filed a formal complaint against him during the hockey india league in january 2025.

Article Title: Parveen Hooda holds her nerve to clinch Asian Games boxing gold in 3-2 thriller
Article Text:
India's Parveen Hooda (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lovlina ends India's 12-year wait

Parveen Hooda completed a remarkable comeback by clinching the women's 65kg boxing gold at the Asian Games , beating Chinese Taipei's Chen Nien-Chen 3-2 in a split decision in a closely fought final.The Indian boxer had to dig deep in the deciding round after Chen levelled the contest following two rounds. Parveen held her nerve in a tense finish, relying on her counter-punching as the Chinese Taipei boxer pressed for the decisive blows.The victory adds another boxing gold for India on a day when Lovlina Borgohain also stood atop the podium.Parveen made a cautious start to the final, with both boxers initially keeping their distance. She found success with her counters before stepping in with combinations, including some effective body shots. The judges awarded her the opening round 5-0.Chen responded in the second round. Parveen continued to use her reach and movement to keep her opponent at bay, but Chen found her range with quick 1-2 combinations and landed enough clean punches to take the round 10-9 on all five cards.With the scores level heading into the final round, Chen came out aggressively and landed a couple of early jabs.Parveen weathered the pressure and began finding openings with quick combinations of her own.The Indian then switched to counter-punching as Chen pushed forward in the closing stages. The strategy proved enough to edge the contest, with Parveen winning the final by a 3-2 split decision.The gold marks a significant turnaround for Parveen, whose medal from the Hangzhou Asian Games was revoked following a doping violation. She had also exited the 2026 Commonwealth Games at the quarterfinal stage.Chen, a former world champion, came into the final as the 2026 Asian Championships gold medallist and had also won bronze at the previous Asian Games and the Paris Olympics.Earlier on Friday, Lovlina Borgohain ended India's 12-year wait for an Asian Games women's boxing gold by defeating China's Ziyi Bao in the women's 75kg final.The Olympic bronze medallist secured a 5-0 unanimous decision to upgrade the silver medal she won at the previous edition, giving herself a gold medal on her birthday.Lovlina became only the second Indian woman after MC Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing gold. Mary Kom had claimed the 51kg title at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.
Article Summary: Lovlina borgohain ends india's 12-year wait for an asian games women's boxing gold by defeating china's ziyi bao in the women's 75kg final. Parveen hooda completed a remarkable comeback by clinching thewomen's 65kg boxing gold at the asian games. The indian boxer had to dig deep in the deciding round after chen levelled the contest following two rounds.

India’s medal-winning campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 has reached 80 medals, with the contingent winning 18 gold, 26 silver and 36 bronze medals. India are currently fifth in the overall medal standings.India’s medal tally received a major boost over the last two days, with the contingent adding gold medals across boxing, wrestling, archery, hockey and golf. Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal, Sujeet Kalkal, the Indian women’s hockey team, Kumkum Mohod and Pranavi Urs have all contributed gold medals to India’s latest surge.Kumkum also won silver alongside Dhiraj Bommadevara in the mixed recurve team event, while India’s women’s golf team of Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar secured silver.On October 3, Kumkum Mohod added another gold by winning the women’s individual recurve event. The 17-year-old defeated South Korea’s Oh Yejin 6-5 in a shoot-off to become the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. Her victory also secured an Olympic quota place for India for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.Pranavi Urs also scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to win individual golf gold at the Asian Games, while helping India claim silver in the women’s team event alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.India’s women’s cricket team won the country’s first gold medal of the Games after defeating Sri Lanka in the final. Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet then added India’s second gold by winning the 10m air pistol mixed team event.India subsequently won both the men’s and women’s kabaddi titles, while Neeru Dhanda secured gold in the women’s trap event. She later teamed up with Kynan Chenai to win the mixed trap team gold.In athletics, Kiran Pahal, Poovamma Machettira, Prachi Choudhary and Vithya Ramraj won gold in the women’s 4x400m relay. India also dominated the compound archery events, winning gold in the men’s team, women’s team and mixed team events.On October 2, Lovlina Borgohain defeated China’s Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final to win gold. The victory came on her birthday and made Lovlina only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games gold.The women’s recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod then created history by defeating South Korea 5-3 to win India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the event.India then added three more gold medals in boxing and wrestling, with Parveen Hooda winning the women’s 65kg title, Ankush Panghal taking gold in the men’s 80kg category and Sujeet Kalkal winning the men’s freestyle 65kg event.The Indian women’s hockey team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold by defeating China 1-0 in the final, with the victory also securing a direct qualification spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.On October 3, Kumkum completed a memorable Asian Games campaign by winning individual recurve gold. After being pushed to a shoot-off by Oh Yejin, the 17-year-old held her nerve to shoot a 10 and beat the South Korean 8, securing India’s first individual women’s recurve gold at the Asian Games.Pranavi Urs added another historic gold in golf. The 23-year-old became the first Indian woman to win an individual golf gold medal at the Asian Games. She also helped India win silver in the women’s team event.India’s silver medal haul has come across shooting, athletics, weightlifting, wushu, squash, wrestling, sailing, archery and golf.The shooting contingent has been one of India’s biggest contributors, with medals across air rifle, 50m rifle 3 positions, 25m pistol and trap events.Mirabai Chanu ended her long wait for an Asian Games medal by taking silver in the women’s 49kg weightlifting event, while Roshibina Devi won silver in women’s 60kg sanda. Gulveer Singh also enjoyed a strong Games, winning silver in the men’s 10,000m and 1500m events.In squash, Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh won silver in the women’s and men’s singles events respectively. India also collected silver medals in sailing and archery, with Prince Noble Kurisinkal and Manu Francis finishing second in the men’s skiff.Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara lost to China in the mixed recurve final, while Dhiraj Bommadevara, Neeraj Chauhan and Yashdeep Bhoge finished runners-up to South Korea in the men’s recurve team event.The latest addition came in golf, where Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar won silver in the women’s team event. China took gold, while India finished second.India’s bronze medals have come from a wide range of disciplines, including shooting, athletics, squash, boxing, wrestling, archery, sailing, sepaktakraw, badminton, rowing, table tennis, kurash, soft tennis and mixed martial arts.Athletics has produced a large share of India’s bronze medals, with Parul Chaudhary, Gulveer Singh, Tejaswin Shankar, Vithya Ramraj, Pooja Singh, Rohit Yadav and others contributing to the tally.India’s squash contingent has also produced multiple medals, with Joshna Chinappa, Velavan Senthilkumar, Anahat Singh, Tanvi Khanna, Abhay Singh and Veer Chotrani contributing across the mixed doubles and team events.In boxing, Narender Berwal, Priya Ghanghas and Kapil Pokhariya won bronze, while Sunil Kumar secured bronze in Greco-Roman wrestling.Nethra Kumanan won bronze in the women’s dinghy sailing event, while India’s men’s quadrant team secured bronze in sepaktakraw after losing 0-2 to Japan in the semifinal.
Article Summary: India's women's hockey team clinch gold at asian games 2026. India's men's kabaddi team also won a gold medal in the men's tournament. India’s silver medal winners were elavenil valarivan, sonam maskar, vidarsa vinod. Aishwary pratap singh tomar, rudrankksh patil, niraj kumar shooting men’s 50m rifle 3 positions team.

Article Title: Mumbai allrounder Suryansh Shedge replaces injured Hardik Pandya in India A squad for Australia A ODIs
Article Text:
Suryansh Shedge (Image: IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Mumbai's young all-rounder Suryansh Shedge has replaced injured India all-rounder Hardik Pandya in the India A squad, which will play three one-dayers against Australia A from Tuesday in Puducherry “Shedge had gone to the BCCI 's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru for a fitness assessment, and after being cleared by the CoE's medical team, left for Puducherry yesterday,” a source tracking developments told TOI on Sunday. The matches are scheduled for October 6, 9 and 11.Hardik Pandya has reportedly experienced discomfort in his right calf. Pandya became aware of the issue after undergoing a fitness assessment on September 19. An MRI after the assessment revealed very mild intramedullary oedema, which is consistent with right medial tibial stress syndrome.The development means Shedge will miss Mumbai's Ranji Trophy opener against Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium from October 11.A minor quadriceps injury had kept the 23-year-old out of action lately, but the all-rounder is now fit to return to action.Shedge played three T20Is for India during the tours of Ireland, England and Zimbabwe in June-July.However, he missed out on being named in the India and Rest of India squads due to his injury and also did not feature in any of Mumbai's pre-season tournaments.Shedge performed impressively for India A in a tri-series in Sri Lanka in June. Batting in the middle order, the 23-year-old scored 147 runs in five matches and also chipped in with the ball, bowling 23 overs across the tournament.He was also one of the standout performers for Mumbai in their victorious Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy campaign in 2024-25, scoring 131 runs at a strike rate of 251.92 in the lower middle order.
Article Summary: Suryansh shedge has replaced injured india all-rounder hardik pandya in the india a squad. India a will play three one-dayers against australia a from tuesday in puducherry. The 23-year-old will miss mumbai's ranji trophy opener against chandigarh.
